ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (dark) surface with approximately 15% high-intensity (white) pixels localized at the distal tips and along portions of the trailing edge.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Vast central low-intensity (black/dark grey) region. High-intensity (white) mottling and contiguous geometric patches localized at the extreme distal tips (left and right). Discrete high-contrast circular clusters concentrated at the terminal edges.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, narrow V-shaped central depression with a calculated pixel angle of approximately 52 degrees and a bounding-box depth relative to lobe height of 1:4.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, low-amplitude serrations (peaks < 10 pixels) across 80% of the boundary. Notable deep irregularities and larger indentations located on the inner-third of the left lobe trailing edge.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Complex sigmoidal curve; concave trajectory immediately following the median notch, transitioning to a broad convex sweep towards the distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense spatial clusters of high-contrast, roughly circular white-on-black pixel groups concentrated on the outer distal edges of both lobes, corresponding to barnacle attachment sites.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Two distinct parallel dark-on-white linear disruptions (rake-like marks) visible on the high-intensity patch of the upper-left distal lobe tip.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent irregular notch/missing tissue section on the upper trailing edge of the left lobe; extensive distal barnacle colonization and associated white scarring patterns on both tips.
other_distinctive_markers: A singular, isolated high-contrast dark circular spot (focal point) located in the upper-right distal region, surrounded by high-intensity pixel mottling.
